languages_frameworks: mcp>=1.0.0 listed (but the 'MCP server' is a plain class, not the SDK)

implemented_capabilities.capability: Blast radius, betweenness centrality and shortest path via NetworkX over a graph exported from FalkorDB
implemented_capabilities.notes: Pulls all nodes and edges with MATCH (n)/(a)-[r]->(b) into a networkx.DiGraph and runs reverse single_source_shortest_path_length with cutoff for blast radius, nx.betweenness_centrality (is_choke_point if >0.15), and tries Cypher shortestPath before an undirected nx fallback. The README claim of 'GraphBLAS algorithms' is not backed by code: no FalkorDB algo.* call is made.

implemented_capabilities.capability: Ephemeral sandbox graph clone for rehearsal
implemented_capabilities.notes: clone_graph really copies nodes then edges into a new graph by row-by-row Cypher (slow, id/name matching, fragile) and deletes it after; but the 'rehearsal' only deletes DEPLOYED_TO edges and then sets rehearsal_verified = True unconditionally (no health or deadlock check).

Only the first Cypher (Alert->Service) and a shortest-path call are executed. query_pods, query_commits and query_rfc are defined as strings but never run, and the returned 'findings' (commit 7f9a2b, Devon Miller, RFC-104, confidence 0.98, falkordb_queries_executed: 4) are hard-coded literals. Service id defaults to 'svc_auth' if the query returns nothing.

implemented_capabilities.capability: Company-brain decision lineage and ownership agent
implemented_capabilities.notes: Three Cypher strings are declared and never executed; the returned context dict (owners, RFC-104, SecurityBoard approval date, on-call names) is a hard-coded literal.

A fixed 9-step script with asyncio.sleep delays that yields pre-written status messages (e.g. 'Traversing 4 hops...' appears before the triage call). Not an LLM planner. The optional LLM call only produces a commentary string.

Calls the real centrality and blast-radius functions but then attaches hard-coded values: revenue burn 4850/500 USD per minute, impact_level 'SEV-1 CATASTROPHIC', critical_path_affected list, and a fallback centrality 0.38 if the node is not in top-10.

implemented_capabilities.capability: Cypher console and MCP-style tool endpoints
implemented_capabilities.notes: Four tool definitions (query, blast radius, shortest path, clone sandbox) dispatched in-process by a REST endpoint; not an actual MCP protocol server (no stdio/SSE transport, SDK unused).

Real httpx POST to the GitHub pulls API if GITHUB_TOKEN+repo are set (it assumes a pre-existing hotfix branch and never creates one or a commit), otherwise returns a simulated PR #104; Slack webhook POST real if configured, else simulated. The PR body diff is a hard-coded Terraform snippet.
When FalkorDB is unreachable every query returns the whole node/edge list regardless of Cypher; graph content is a hard-coded demo topology.

graph_models_and_cypher: Master graph 'enterprise_master' and 'agent_procedural_memory'. Labels (schema.py): Service, Database, Pod, Commit, Engineer, Incident, Alert, IAMRole, Decision, RunbookStep, Team. Edges: DEPENDS_ON, CONNECTS_TO, RUNS_ON, DEPLOYED_TO, AUTHORED_BY, TRIGGERED_BY, AFFECTS, ASSUMES_ROLE, ENFORCED_IN (Decision->Commit), DISCUSSED_IN, ON_SUCCESS, ON_FAILURE, MEMBER_OF. Procedural memory writes IncidentRecord-[:RESOLVED_VIA]->RunbookResolution. Cypher is simple; queries read p.properties.phase style nested properties inconsistent with how nodes are stored. Uses shortestPath() variable-length; no APOC/GDS and no algo.* despite README claims.
algorithms: Reverse single-source BFS with cutoff for blast radius (algorithms.py:compute_blast_radius, networkx)
Cypher shortestPath with undirected networkx fallback
frontend_interfaces: Next.js 16: app/page.tsx, components GraphVisualizer (force-directed canvas), AgentThoughtStream, BlastRadiusPanel, CompanyBrainPanel, CypherConsole, RemediationModal; Aceternity-style ui components
agent_or_memory_mechanisms: README claims tri-layer memory and procedural runbook DAG. Code: only RemediationAgent._record_procedural_memory writes one IncidentRecord/RunbookResolution pair with hard-coded step name; no recall, no episodic or semantic retrieval, no handoff beyond sequential function calls in the swarm script.
tests_present: none (no tests directory or test files)
dependency_requirements: httpx (used but not listed in requirements.txt)
security_findings: backend/app/main.py:105-108 - POST /api/graph/query executes arbitrary caller-supplied Cypher (including DELETE/CREATE) against any graph name with no authentication.

backend/app/mcp/falkor_mcp_server.py:75-86 and main.py POST /api/mcp/call - falkor_query_cypher and falkor_clone_sandbox_graph reachable unauthenticated; sandbox_name is unvalidated and clone_graph deletes any existing graph of that name (dst.delete()) so an attacker can wipe any graph.

backend/app/graph/falkor_client.py:106,120 - label and relationship type names from existing graph data are interpolated into Cypher f-strings during clone_graph (CREATE (:{lbl} ...), -[:{rel_type} ...]); injectable if graph content is attacker-controlled.
backend/app/agents/llm_client.py:35 - Gemini API key is placed in the request URL query string (?key=...), which can leak into httpx/proxy logs; Anthropic/OpenAI keys correctly in headers.

backend/app/integrations/github_client.py:41-58 - uses a GITHUB_TOKEN to POST pull requests to the configured repo; text is partly built from caller-controlled commit_sha/incident_id (only the fixed demo path passes them today).
backend/app/config.py:15 - default GITHUB_REPO 'mock-enterprise/cloud-infra'; no hard-coded secrets found; .env.example has placeholders only.
docker-compose.yml - FalkorDB (latest tag) and browser exposed on 6379/3000 without auth.
duplicates_or_overlaps: Overlaps blast-radius traversal and SRE incident RCA repos (many in the same hackathon). Its distinctive ideas (clone-graph sandbox rehearsal, decision lineage Commit<-Decision) are mostly slideware in this implementation.
evidence_drift_relevance: LOW - Models Decision-[:ENFORCED_IN]->Commit lineage and a rehearsal sandbox, but the agents return hard-coded results, rehearsal verification is an unconditional True, and there is no versioning, supersession, invalidation or real approval gate.

strongest_reusable_unit.why: A compact export-to-NetworkX pattern giving depth-bounded reverse-reachability and betweenness without GDS; trivially reimplemented. The clone_graph idea (sandbox what-if on a copy) is conceptually useful but the implementation is slow and should use GRAPH.COPY.
strongest_reusable_unit.external_runtime_needed: FalkorDB for data load, networkx; no LLM key required

strategy_rationale: Most 'agent' output is hard-coded demo narrative around a fixed incident (commit 7f9a2b, RFC-104), so little can be reused as an engine; keep it as a reference for the sandbox-clone what-if idea and NetworkX blast radius. No LICENSE file.
